blocks.text: **The problem.** Given a valid **prefix** expression (operator **before** its operands), convert it to **postfix** (operator **after** its operands). Operands are single letters or digits; operators are `+ - * / ^`. For example, `*+AB-CD` becomes `AB+CD-*`.

blocks.alt: One expression tree, two readings. The tree has * at the root, + with A and B on the left, - with C and D on the right. Pre-order reading gives the prefix * + A B - C D; post-order reading gives the postfix A B + C D - *.

blocks.code:
Input:  "*+AB-CD"        Output: "AB+CD-*"
Input:  "*-A/BC-/AKL"    Output: "ABC/-AK/L-*"
Input:  "A"              Output: "A"

blocks.text: Neither prefix nor postfix needs brackets, so no brackets appear anywhere. Each operator just has to move from **before** its two operands to **after** them — and its operands may themselves be whole expressions.
1. Brute force: rewrite the innermost operator, again and again

Find an operator followed directly by two **finished** operands, like `+AB`, and replace those three items with one finished piece written in postfix: `AB+`. Repeat until one piece is left. (Pieces must be tracked as **items**, not loose characters — `AB+` is one operand now, even though it contains an operator symbol.)

blocks.alt: Rewriting * + A B - C D. + A B becomes the piece AB+. Then - C D becomes CD-. Finally * with the pieces AB+ and CD- becomes AB+CD-*.

elements.text: AB+ is a single operand now
elements.originalText: AB+ is a single operand now

blocks.text: **Time O(n²), space O(n).** One rescan per operator.
2. Optimal: recursion reads the structure directly

Read from the left. An operand is a complete expression on its own. An operator is followed by its left operand and then its right operand, so **build each one recursively** and return `left + right + operator`.
**Time O(n), space O(n)** for the recursion — and the same risk of overflowing the call stack on very deep expressions.
3. Best solution: an explicit stack, reading right to left

Exactly the stack from **Prefix to Infix**, with a different way of gluing. Read from the **right**; push operands; for an operator, pop `left` (it's on top, because we read backwards), pop `right`, and push `left + right + operator`.

blocks.alt: Reading * + A B - C D from the right. After reaching +, the stack holds CD- at the bottom, then B, then A on top. + pops left = A and right = B and pushes AB+. Then * pops AB+ and CD- and pushes AB+CD-*.

elements.text:
+ pops left = A, right = B
and pushes AB+
elements.originalText:
+ pops left = A, right = B
and pushes AB+

blocks.caption: The same scan as prefix to infix — only the glue changes.

blocks.text: **Time O(n), space O(n),** iterative. Notice that this solution never needs to know what the operators mean — no precedence, no brackets. Prefix and postfix carry the structure in their order alone.

blocks.alt: Brute force: O(n²) time, O(n) space. Optimal: O(n) time, O(n) calls space. Best: O(n) time, O(n) stack space.

items: **Repeated letters** — `"*AA"` → `"AA*"`: operands are positions, not names.
